A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Advisor Models research. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated in v3. Reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on specialized reasoning, personalization, advisor transfer, and capability retention, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and reports revised RuleArena evaluation, additional Qwen transfer results, and new robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The GRPO-trained advisor, frozen student, natural-language advice, and two-step, three-step, and multi-turn procedures remain unchanged. New student configurations evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds LiveCodeBench Exec beyond the existing SWE repository-repair coverage and tests MTOB under irrelevant review-length advice. Existing datasets and personalization tasks remain. The Qwen transfer experiment adds no documented evaluation language; its presumed training-language mixture concerns the model.

E2.justification: GEPA, PAG, untrained advisors, student-only baselines, oracle prompting, efficient-agent prompting, and direct RL retain their corresponding comparisons. New evaluations use standalone-model baselines; changing the student configuration does not introduce a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 4 replace GPT-5 with GPT-5.2 for RuleArena evaluation. Appendix D.1 adds Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as an MTOB transfer student, and D.5 adds frontier-model tests with an unrelated advisor. Figure 15 inconsistently names GPT-5 mini and GPT-5, leaving that experiment's model matching unclear. Previously specified splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 extends transfer analysis to Qwen72B to investigate transfer across presumed training-distribution differences. New Appendix D.5 examines capability retention with review-length advice on MATH-500, MTOB, and LiveCodeBench Exec using frontier models. These extend existing transfer and robustness questions; earlier ablations and advice examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals and retain the existing significance statements. The added plots follow the same uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run information, or statistical estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces GPT-5 RuleArena accuracy of 31.2%/53.6% without/with advice with GPT-5.2 results of 67.2%/85.6%; this is not a same-model improvement. Figure 11 adds Qwen72B MTOB chrF of 35.2/44.7. New Figure 15 reports baseline/advised values of 0.868/0.866 on MATH-500, 46.2/45.5 chrF on MTOB, and 0.923/0.954 on LiveCodeBench. Other existing numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward definitions in Appendix C and Monte Carlo reward-estimation discussion in Appendix B.3 are unchanged. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claimed 71% RuleArena improvement for GPT-5 with 27.4% for GPT-5.2, and the conclusion updates the percentage accordingly. The central claims about dynamic steering, personalization, transferability, and robustness retain their scope.

C2.justification: V3 interprets Qwen transfer as evidence of transfer across different presumed training distributions. Appendix D.5 adds the explanation that stronger students should better ignore irrelevant advice. The unexplained GPT-5 tax underperformance discussion disappears with the replaced evaluation; existing applicability limits and other interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C and F retain the training parameters, hardware, processing instructions, reward definitions, and prompts. Code-access information is unchanged. V3 does not supply additional sample-selection, prompting, or execution details for the new LiveCodeBench evaluation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds IDPG and distinguishes its instance-specific classification soft prompts from natural-language advice. V3 also adds the GPT-5.2 reference. Other reference changes largely update metadata for already cited works rather than expand research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose additions, adds Appendix D.5 and a generic Impact Statement, updates author and conference information, revises acknowledgements, and edits bibliographic metadata. The main section organization and method narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 11 gains a fourth panel for Qwen72B, and Figure 15 adds three robustness panels. Figure 4 changes its RuleArena student label, while Figures 3–5 move with text reflow. The tables and remaining figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Qwen72B transfer result and IDPG comparison modestly strengthen the paper's generalization evidence and positioning. The broader robustness tests offer additional support, but Figure 15's conflicting GPT-5 mini/GPT-5 labels and missing LiveCodeBench settings limit their evidential value. V3 also leaves GPT-5 attached to the new GPT-5.2 tax numbers in the introduction. These reporting weaknesses temper the gains without undermining the retained method and experiments.
